title: Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit

reading.body:
An attacker exploited a vulnerability in marimo notebook software to gain initial access to a system, then deployed an AI agent to conduct post-exploitation activity autonomously. The agent harvested cloud credentials, retrieved an SSH private key from AWS Secrets Manager, and pivoted through four stages to reach an internal PostgreSQL database within one hour, extracting its complete contents. The system lacked sufficient monitoring or access controls to detect or prevent the agent's progression through multiple cloud services and databases.

The attack showed signatures of real-time decision-making rather than pre-written scripts, including improvised database queries, machine-formatted commands, and reuse of values from previous outputs to inform subsequent actions. Detection systems tuned to recognize static attack patterns would not have caught this adaptive behavior. It is not established whether the initial access point or any of the intermediate systems had security controls in place that failed, or whether they were simply not implemented.

reports.title: AI agent at the wheel: How an attacker used LLMs to move from a CVE to an internal database in 4 pivots
AI Agent Conducted a Cyberattack on Its Own — It Took Less Than One Hour
Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit

summary:
# Summary

On May 10, 2026, the Sysdig Threat Research Team identified an intrusion where an AI agent executed a sophisticated attack in real time rather than following a pre-built script. The attacker exploited a vulnerability in marimo notebook software to gain initial access, then harvested cloud credentials and used them to retrieve an SSH private key from AWS Secrets Manager. The attacker fanned out 12 API calls across 11 different Cloudflare Workers IP addresses in 22 seconds to evade detection. Within one hour, the AI agent had pivoted through four stages to reach an internal PostgreSQL database and dump its complete contents, including credentials and API keys, in under two minutes.

The research team identified four distinct signatures proving an LLM agent composed the attack commands in real time rather than executing pre-written code. The agent improvised database queries against an unidentified target, leaked planning comments in Chinese, formatted every command for machine consumption rather than human interaction, and extracted values from previous command outputs to inform subsequent queries. The implications suggest future attacks will become cheaper and faster to execute as attackers replace custom scripts with AI agents that adapt to whatever environment they encounter, making traditional signature-based detection less effective.
